positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
•   Collaborated with 15 undergraduates, 2 graduate students, and 2 professors from various Universities to investigate the representation of male and female scholars and address implicit biases that may exist

•   Coded 912 graduate syllabi and 66 Ph.D. reading lists across the four subfields of political science by sifting through thousands of pages to create datasets to better represent and prove our research thesis

•   Assisted in identifying gender implicit biases in publications and citations in political science graduate training to bring awareness to gender biases in political science that have never been discussed before

Abstract:
This project will investigate the representation of male and female scholars in the training of political science doctoral students. Graduate syllabi and comprehensive exam reading lists will be collected in order to establish an original, publicly-available database of works assigned to political science doctoral students from across the subfields of political science. The database will be used to examine two questions: (1) To what extent are female scholars represented in assigned works? (2) What factors affect variation in gender representation in the works that faculty and graduate programs assign?. Factors hypothesized to affect rates of assigning female authors include instructor gender, age, race/ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, academic rank and years in the profession. The project will also produce free, open-source software to convert syllabi text into a CSV formatted list and to code the genders of authors.
